title: Joel And I — Chas Lessons #3 (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar dry wit spoken word cabaret 104bpm upright bass brushed snare deadpan warm baritone male vocal observational character portrait grammar lesson Swan River
lyrics:
[Intro - piano bar, unhurried, expectant]
Swan River. Late afternoon.
Two boys heading down to the water.

[Verse 1]
Corey said to his dad
"Me and Joel are going down"
Chas waited a half-beat
The way a man waits
When he knows exactly what he wants to say
And is deciding how to say it

[Verse 2]
Not a lecture
Not a big speech about grammar
Not a whiteboard and a pointing stick
Just: "Oh — you mean Joel and I"
That's all
Clean
Landed soft
Stuck hard

[Chorus]
Joel and I
Not me and Joel
Joel and I
Take out the other name and read what's left
Me am going to the water
Wrong
I am going to the water
Right
So it's Joel and I
Every time
Joel and I

[Bridge - spoken, level, warm]
Remove the other name.
That's the test.
"Me and my team built this" — take out "my team."
"Me built this." Wrong.
"I built this." Right.
So it's "my team and I."
And put yourself last.
The order of your words
is the order of your priorities.
Put yourself last in language
and something shifts.

[Verse 3]
Language is character in advance
How you speak about others before yourself
Is visible before you act
Corey ran that test today
"The team and I" — not "me and the team"
Better still: "The team did this"
Let yourself be last
Let the river prove the rule

[Chorus reprise]
Joel and I
Swan River, one sentence
Joel and I
Permanent
One correction, no lecture
One sentence, no shame
Joel and I
That's the whole lesson
That's the whole lesson

[Outro - piano alone, warm and level]
Corey and Joel went to the water
Joel and Corey went to the water
One of those is right
Chas knew which one
He just said it once
